title: Seastar Systems - Helm/operator marketplace compatibility sync
topics: Helm chart vs operator delivery for marketplace
Signed container images and repo hosting (ECR/GCR)
KMS/HSM integration for secrets and KV cache encryption
Network controls: egress policies, mutual TLS
summary: Redwood AE+SE reviewed Seastar's proposed Helm/operator approach for marketplace packaging. Main concerns: image signing, onboarding flow for private VPC installs, KMS integration for secret material, and metering hooks required by the marketplace. Agreed on a pilot using a signed Helm chart + operator for lifecycle management and an S3-backed artifact bucket for charts. Action items assigned to share repo links, security docs, and a short deploy checklist for the marketplace review board.
action_items: Owner: Ravi Patel; Item: Share sample Helm chart repo and operator CRD examples; Due: 2026-11-23
Owner: Lisa Chen (Seastar); Item: Provide Seastar SOC2/ISO attestation and SSO SAML metadata; Due: 2026-11-24
Owner: Raj Mehta; Item: Confirm container registry (ECR) repo naming, image signing process (cosign), and access model for marketplace; Due: 2026-11-22
Owner: Carla Nguyen; Item: Send draft marketplace listing metadata template and billing event spec; Due: 2026-11-20
Owner: Marta Lopez; Item: Produce short runbook for in-cluster operator upgrade rollback and safe KV cache migration; Due: 2026-11-30
next_steps: Set up a 1-week pilot cluster for helm + operator install (Redwood SE to provision test environment)
Exchange signed artifact examples (cosign signatures + chart provenance files)
Security teams to run a short checklist before listing window opens (SAML, audit logs, KMS integration)
Schedule a follow-up demo with Marketplace review board on 2026-11-29
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 54m
Attendees: Carla (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Marta (Redwood PM), Jen (Seastar Cloud Architect), Omar (Seastar Platform Eng), Lisa (Seastar Security), Raj (Seastar Partner Ops)

[00:00] Carla: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we've got about 55 minutes on the calendar, so we'll walk through the packaging options and the marketplace requirements from our side. Ravi will lead the tech bits. Quick intro round — maybe just names and roles, then jump in.
[00:18] Jen: Hi I'm Jen, cloud architect at Seastar, working on how we surface our edge inference product as a listed offering.
[00:25] Omar: Omar, platform eng, focused on deployment pipelines and registry access.
[00:29] Lisa: Lisa, security and compliance. I'll be checking off SOC2/Secrets/KMS items.
[00:34] Raj: Raj, partner ops, I'll own the listing metadata and partner portal bits.
[00:38] Carla: Perfect. Marta anything to add?
[00:42] Marta: Yeah hi all, I'm the product PM on the Redwood side for marketplace integrations — I'll help with the listing template and billing hooks.
[00:49] Ravi: Great, ok so first slide, uh I mean first point, we've seen two common patterns for partners: publish a signed Helm chart that installs your container images and optionally an operator CRD for lifecycle ops; or deliver an operator-only bundle that pulls images at runtime. Each has tradeoffs.
[01:10] Omar: Our initial preference was operator-only because we want self-healing and lifecycle upgrades, but we hit friction with marketplace reviewers around image provenance and consent for cross-account pulls.
[01:22] Ravi: Right. Operator-only means the operator needs cross-account registry permissions, or the images need to be mirrored into the customer's registry. That makes the onboarding flow heavier. Helm chart with embedded operator binary + images pre-pulled can be simpler for the marketplace review.
[01:35] Jen: If we go Helm, how do we handle registry access for private VPC installs? Customers won't give us push rights.
[01:42] Ravi: Two options — 1) host images in a public ECR/GCR with signed images and let customers pull (requires org-level allowlist for pulling), or 2) provide a mirrorable image manifest and instructions for customers to pull into their registry. The marketplace typically prefers signed images with provenance.
[01:58] Lisa: On signing, we need details on cosign or sigstore usage, key management, and whether Redwood verifies signatures during install. Do you have an automated verification step in the Helm install?
[02:08] Ravi: We don't enforce it in the user's cluster by default, but for marketplace listings we recommend including a post-install hook that runs a cosign verification against a signed digest, or an admission webhook that validates images before run. We can share a sample hook.
[02:22] Carla: This is good — Raj, is the marketplace review ok with a post-install verification step, or do they require artifact validation on the marketplace side?
[02:30] Raj: The board's preference is that artifacts are signed and verifiable; they prefer evidence in the submission packet. A runtime verification is a plus but not mandatory on day one.
[02:39] Marta: For the listing, we also collect chart provenance, license, and a short security overview — a one-pager that Lisa can sign off on.
[02:47] Lisa: Ok. We will need SOC2 report, SSO metadata for SAML (if you support SSO), and a list of audit logs you can forward to us. Also KMS integration plan for secrets is critical.
[02:58] Jen: About KMS — Seastar currently uses AWS KMS and we also support HashiCorp Vault internally. If Redwood requires an integration for KV cache encryption or secrets during install, what's the recommended approach?
[03:09] Ravi: Two patterns: a) let the operator use customer-managed KMS by passing key ARNs during install (helm values), b) use an external secrets operator that retrieves secrets from the customer's KMS/Vault and populates k8s secrets. For marketplace we favor the first option, plus clear docs around least-privilege IAM policies.
[03:27] Omar: How does Redwood handle the KV cache at runtime when models are served? Any encryption at rest requirements?
[03:33] Marta: Redwood's typical deployment encrypts KV cache on disk with customer KMS when in dedicated/private mode. For hosted listings we require docs showing encryption and lifecycle. We can provide a reference config.
[03:42] Jen: Ok that helps. Next, networking: mutual TLS for control plane calls and egress restrictions — we've been asked to limit outbound ports in regulated customer networks.
[03:53] Ravi: Admission controller + networkpolicy is common. For outbound we recommend using mTLS over 443 and avoid any other egress ports. If you need drain ports for updates there's a small list which we can provide. Also preflight checks during chart install should validate network policies.
[04:12] Lisa: Will your operator require cluster-admin perms? Marketplace security flags that immediately.
[04:17] Ravi: No, the operator is designed to run with limited RBAC but for initial installs some CRD creation requires cluster-level scope. We're exploring a split install: a lightweight chart that creates CRDs and a namespaced operator after that to reduce required permissions. We'll share a privilege minimization doc.
[04:35] Omar: That split install model sounds promising. Does Redwood's marketplace allow a two-step install? Some reviewers said single-click installs are preferred.
[04:42] Raj: One-click is user friendly but not required for listing. The important piece is documented steps and automation scripts — if you provide an install job that creates the CRD first, then flips a namespace, it's acceptable.
[04:55] Carla: Let's talk about billing / metering: Redwood needs a simple hook to emit usage events when your operator provisions model endpoints or when inference tokens are consumed. What events can you expose?
[05:05] Marta: We can emit events at these boundaries: endpoint creation, model load, inference count per minute. We prefer a lightweight metering shim that POSTs to a secure Redwood endpoint with an API key. Is there a spec?
[05:16] Carla: Yes — we'll send a billing event spec. For marketplace we prefer server-side metering via signed events (HMAC), or pull-based metering where Redwood queries a read-only reporting API. Both workable.
[05:29] Raj: For corporate customers, a pull-based model that reads aggregated daily usage is more common. Push is ok for PLG customers.
[05:37] Lisa: From security, any push-based event must be over TLS and we should validate signatures; no secret keys in cleartext.
[05:45] Ravi: We'll make the shim use short-lived tokens and sign payloads. We'll include sample code in the repo.
[05:52] Jen: A quick question about images: will Redwood scan images pre-listing? Some marketplaces require vulnerability scans.
[05:58] Carla: We do basic scanning as part of the listing process and recommend partners run a SBOM scan. We'll share the scanning reports required by the marketplace board.
[06:08] Omar: Noted. Next — CI/CD: for operator updates we want canary rollouts. How does Redwood handle canary versions in marketplace contexts?
[06:16] Ravi: Marketplace listings can specify supported minor versions; for operator updates the marketplace can allow a canary channel. The operator should implement owner-referenced rollout policies and a safe rollback API. Marta will include canary guidance in the listing template.
[06:28] Marta: Also include a health-check endpoint for the operator and Liveness/Readiness probes. The review board checks those.
[06:34] Lisa: About audit logs — we need to know which events are logged and retention period. Does Redwood forward install/upgrade audit logs to the partner?
[06:42] Ravi: For dedicated/private deployments, we can stream audit logs to your S3 or partner destination. For hosted, we capture audit logs and provide a 90-day export; longer retention is an add-on. We'll document the schema.
[06:55] Jen: Great. Raj, on the listing metadata, what about prebuilt values for different cloud providers? Customers want one-click for AWS, GCP, AKS.
[07:04] Raj: We encourage partners to supply provider-specific values.yaml files and validated manifests for each supported platform. That reduces support friction.
[07:12] Omar: Ok we'll prepare per-cloud manifests. Quick note: image registry — we plan to use ECR with cross-account pull roles. Raj, is that acceptable?
[07:21] Raj: ECR is fine; please document the cross-account policy and provide role ARNs. Ensure signed images and proper tags.
[07:28] Lisa: We'll also need guidance on rotating keys for cosign and a process for revoking compromised images.
[07:34] Ravi: We'll demonstrate using cosign with ephemeral keys and publish a revoke list; samples in repo.
[07:41] Jen: On the operator side — does Redwood provide a library of controller-runtime patterns or an example CRD template to match marketplace expectations?
[07:49] Ravi: Yes, we've got a partner-operator starter repo with example CRDs and controllers that follow our spec for lifecycle hooks and metering. We'll share link after the call.
[07:59] Carla: Perfect. I'm going to call out a few items we'll add as checkboxes in the partner onboarding packet: signed images, SOC2 + SSO metadata, chart provenance, network policy recommendations, RBAC declartion, billing events spec, and sample operator CRD.
[08:15] Marta: Also, include a short runbook for rollback and KV migration procedures. That was flagged earlier.
[08:21] Omar: On KV migration — we run a small in-cluster RocksDB for KV cache. During upgrades we need a graceful migration path to avoid cache corruption. Any pointers?
[08:31] Ravi: We recommend snapshot + restore semantics and versioned cache keys; the operator should expose a safe drain API that flushes and snapshots cache before schema change. Marta will write the suggested pattern.
[08:45] Lisa: Switching to compliance — SSO: does Seastar support IdP-initiated SAML? We'll need metadata and a test account.
[08:53] Jen: Yes we support both IdP and SP initiated flows. We'll provide a test SP metadata file.
[08:58] Carla: Good. Before we run out of time let's surface anything blocking for the pilot. Raj?
[09:04] Raj: Main blockers are: signed image proof, SOC2 docs, and an install that doesn't require cluster-admin for day-1. If you can show the split install pattern and key artifacts we'll push to review board.
[09:16] Carla: Actionable, we'll try to get the split-install example and repo out this week. Ravi will push the helm/operator samples.
[09:23] Ravi: I'll also include a sample admission webhook for cosign verification and a minimal RBAC manifest.
[09:30] Jen: One more question — runtime secrets: do you store model keys in plain k8s secrets? We need encryption at rest and control plane separation.
[09:38] Marta: For marketplace we require that secret material is either stored encrypted via customer-managed KMS or fetched at runtime via an external secrets mechanism. We discourage storing cleartext secrets in k8s.
[09:49] Lisa: Can we see how Redwood does key rotation? That will be part of the security checklist.
[09:55] Ravi: We'll include our rotation guide. It's based on short-lived tokens + automated rotation jobs that re-encrypt persisted cache with new keys.
[10:05] Omar: Thanks, that helps. Quick logistical question — what artifacts do you want in the initial listing packet? Raj?
[10:11] Raj: Minimum: chart tgz with provenance, SBOM, signed container digest proof, SOC2 summary, SSO metadata, per-cloud values files, and a short install/rollback runbook.
[10:24] Carla: We'll follow that list. Any competing vendor behavior we should call out that influences listing choices? Raj or Jen?
[10:31] Jen: Some vendors require customers to mirror images into their own registries to avoid cross-account pulls — that's more friction. We prefer minimizing that step.
[10:38] Raj: Also note that EdgeServe had a UI-first listing requiring a webhook for metering; that's more complex. We usually advise partners to keep metering optional on day one.
[10:47] Marta: Alright let's recap and close with next steps.
[10:51] Carla: Recap: Ravi share helm/operator repo + cosign hook (due 11/23), Carla to send marketplace listing template & billing spec (due 11/20), Seastar to share SOC2 + SAML metadata (due 11/24), Raj confirm ECR details (due 11/22), Marta produce KV cache migration runbook (due 11/30). We'll set up a pilot cluster and schedule a follow-up with the marketplace review board for 2026-11-29.
[11:18] Jen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[11:22] Lisa: Thanks, and I'll send an initial checklist to Carla offline.
[11:25] Carla: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and a calendar invite for the 11/29 slot. Bye.
